epidural-response.rendering: Original PDF retained unchanged as an input for docs/traces.

intracortical-response.rendering: Original PDF retained unchanged as an input for docs/traces.

noise-response.rendering: Original PDF retained unchanged as an input for docs/traces.

reported-changes.rendering: Bar chart of the reported percent changes drawn as SVG with the page's stylesheet and rendered with headless Edge by docs/traces/render_readme_figures.py, in GitHub's light and dark themes; no data reanalysis.

interactive-traces.source: Vector paths of epidural-, intracortical- and noise-response-original.pdf, read by docs/traces/build_data.py.
interactive-traces.method: Axes calibrated from tick marks and labels; each path assigned to its electrode by MNE's spatial colour for the montage in general/loader.py (µECoG) or montage_remap('Experiment 09') in preprocessing_MEA/utils.py (MEA), checked against the figure legends. Path vertices lie on a 2034.5 Hz grid (24414 Hz decimated by 12); traces are linearly resampled onto that grid and stored as int16 in 0.1 µV.
interactive-traces.flags: RANSAC bad-epoch logs are the figures' rasterised heatmaps sampled at each channel's centre: 233 rows for 600 epochs (epidural, noise) and 227 rows for 240 epochs (intracortical).
interactive-traces.scientific_changes: None. No recording is reanalysed; precision is limited to the published figures.

steps-animation.rendering: Frames of docs/index.html in capture mode (?capture&mode=epidural&theme=light|dark) sampled every 100 ms along the page's step timeline with headless Edge by docs/traces/render_readme_figures.py. Backgrounds match GitHub's light (#ffffff) and dark (#0d1117) themes.
steps-animation.method: Steps 1-4 replay autoreject's Ransac on the averaged response: seeded random subsets of round(min_channels x channels) contacts, inverse-distance-weighted prediction in place of spherical splines, median over subsets, uncentred correlation against min_corr. Step 5 uses the paper's bad-epoch log; step 6 the paper's RANSAC output. Blends between states are visual transitions.
